original_question: Assume an overcomplete Gabor frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} admits an ordering {f_k} for which {f_k}_{k in I} = {T^k phi}_{k in I} with bounded T. Must such a bounded-operator representation exist for both indexing choices I=N_0={0,1,2,...} and I=Z, or can the existence of a bounded representation depend on whether the ordered orbit is one-sided or two-sided?
target_in_paper: Section 1's open Gabor-frame orbit question, centered on Conjecture 1.1 and read together with Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3: for a fixed index set I in {N_0, Z}, does an overcomplete Gabor frame admit an ordering that is an orbit {T^k phi}_{k in I} of a bounded operator? The nearby results are used to explain that the index set matters, so the paper treats the N_0 and Z cases separately rather than asking whether one implies the other. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.00480))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main mathematical object (an overcomplete Gabor frame), the sought representation as an ordered operator orbit with bounded T, and the relevance of the two possible index sets I = N_0 and I = Z. It is also in the right conceptual neighborhood of the paper, because the paper explicitly stresses that changing the indexing from N_0 to Z creates a genuinely different problem. ([backend.orbit.dtu.dk](https://backend.orbit.dtu.dk/ws/files/197987573/Frame_representations.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient Hilbert space L^2(R) should be stated explicitly.
The Gabor frame should be introduced as G(g,a,b) = {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} with g in L^2(R) and a,b > 0.
The question in the paper is existential for a fixed index set I, not conditional on first assuming that a bounded representation already exists for one indexing.

The paper does not formulate the issue as: if a bounded representation exists for I = N_0, must one also exist for I = Z (or conversely)? That implication is your extrapolation, not the paper's official formulation.
The phrase "admits an ordering" should be made precise: one chooses a bijective enumeration of the doubly indexed Gabor family by the chosen countable index set I.

For the two-sided case I = Z, one must specify how negative iterates T^k are defined; equivalently, T must be invertible at least on the orbit span, and this should be built into a stand-alone formulation.

The paper's nearby context uses Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 to show that bounded-orbit representability can depend on the indexing set already for other frame classes, so that context should be reflected rather than folded into the Gabor question itself.
If the goal is to stay closest to the paper, the question should ask about existence of such a bounded-orbit representation for a chosen I in {N_0, Z}, not about dependence between the two cases.
refined_question: Fix I in {N_0, Z}. Let g in L^2(R) and a,b > 0 be such that the Gabor system G(g,a,b) = {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} is an overcomplete frame for L^2(R). Does there exist an ordering {f_k}_{k in I} of the elements of G(g,a,b), a vector phi in L^2(R), and a bounded linear operator T on L^2(R) (for I = Z, with the negative iterates T^k well defined on the orbit span) such that f_k = T^k phi for every k in I?
justification: The draft is close to the paper's theme but it blends two neighboring items: (1) the paper's actual Gabor-frame open problem, which is an existence question for a chosen index set I, and (2) the contextual observation that the possibility of a bounded-orbit representation can depend on whether one uses N_0 or Z. The latter point is exactly why Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 are emphasized nearby; they motivate treating the Gabor question separately for the one-sided and two-sided indexings. So the sharp paper-faithful rewrite should be a fixed-I existence question, not a cross-implication question between the N_0 and Z cases.
